subject: Possible to shoehorn shapes into a guide_legend used for linetypes?

messages.author: dd6646899d689f77
messages.subject: Possible to shoehorn shapes into a guide_legend used for linetypes?
parts:
Dear list users,

Please consider the code below:

library(ggplot2)
data = structure(list(vowel = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L,
8L, 9L, 1L, 2L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 8L), .Label = c("2:", "9y", "a:",
"Au", "e:", "Ei", "i", "o:", "u"), class = "factor"), rel_frame = c(1L,
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), f1 = c(356.396954839706,
523.513796448639, 823.1085896871, 575.950481447045, 351.651881467446,
517.089619543663, 266.225003126744, 387.739580773335, 312.833669505029,
391.613850900754, 395.507781094284, 404.527669763935, 328.964713375543,
447.290410360164, 417.10520571584), f2 = c(1604.78039782924,
1601.03182911306, 1579.75747215015, 1180.80473193673, 2317.10076880879,
2077.33134310296, 2394.21184958644, 847.417832375575, 1013.80411107007,
1687.7356515113, 1837.98866401878, 949.165650424203, 2414.67446214708,
2325.84168538597, 1019.8690180562)), .Names = c("vowel", "rel_frame",
"f1", "f2"), row.names = c(136L, 144L, 152L, 160L, 168L, 176L,
184L, 192L, 200L, 208L, 216L, 232L, 240L, 248L, 264L), class = "data.frame")
data$rel_frame = as.factor(data$rel_frame)
i = data[data$vowel == 'i',]
u = data[data$vowel == 'u',]
a = data[data$vowel == 'a:',]
drest = data[!data$vowel %in% c('u','i','a:'),]
p = ggplot(data=drest,aes(f2,f1,shape=rel_frame,group=vowel,linetype=vowel))
p = p + geom_point(data=a,shape=0) + geom_point(data=i,shape=1) + geom_point(data=u,shape=2)
p = p + scale_linetype(name='Vowel',breaks=vbreaks)
p = p + scale_shape_manual(name='Timepoint',breaks=c(1,2),values=c(16,17))
p = p + geom_point(size=3) + geom_line(size=1)
p = p + scale_x_reverse() + scale_y_reverse()
p = p + guides(linetype=guide_legend(override.aes=list(shape=c(0,1,2,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA),linetype=c(0,0,0,1,2,3,4,5,6))))
p

These are vowel data, and they're not particularly exciting unless you're a linguist. If you plot the data per the above commands, you can see that I measured nine vowels, of which the middle six have two observations each, whereas the three vowels in the corner (i,u,a:) have one observation each (these vowels are reference points).
For the vowels which have two observations, I use shapes to distinguish observation 1 from observation 2, and I use different linetypes to distinguish the different vowels. For the vowels that have only one observation, I obviously can't use different linetypes because there is no line, so I used different shapes instead.

This all looks very nice, but now I want to add these three custom shapes coming from these three manually-inserted vowels to the legend for the vowels. This StackOverflow suggestion - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16311335/different-legend-keys-inside-same-legend-in-ggplot2 - suggests using guide_legend with override_aes, but it is not working the way I was hoping it would: I am successfully managing to remove the (phantom) linetypes for the three manually-inserted vowels, but I cannot seem to replace them with their respective shape symbols.
Is there a way to achieve that nonetheless? In other words: the blank spaces in the legend for 'i', 'u', 'a:' should be replaced by the open circle, open triangle, and open square you can see in the top left, top right, and bottom middle of the plot.

Many thanks,
Cesko
